stem: A company needs virtual servers where it controls the operating system and installed software.

options.why: Fargate runs containers without giving you control of the host operating system.
Lightsail container services run containers without OS-level control of the servers.
EC2 provides resizable virtual servers with full OS control.
Lambda runs functions without OS access.

explanation.answer: Amazon EC2 provides virtual servers (instances) where you choose the OS, instance type and software.
explanation.concept: EC2 is infrastructure as a service: more control, more management.
explanation.examTip: Virtual servers with OS control = EC2.

stem: A company runs an in-memory analytics workload that needs a lot of RAM relative to CPU.
prompt: Which EC2 instance family fits BEST?

options.why: Storage optimized instances focus on high local disk I/O.
Compute optimized instances have high CPU relative to memory.
These include GPUs for graphics or ML, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Memory optimized instances are designed for large in-memory datasets.

explanation.answer: Memory optimized instances deliver fast performance for workloads that process large datasets in memory.
explanation.concept: Families: general purpose (M, T), compute (C), memory (R, X), storage (I, D), accelerated (P, G, Inf, Trn).

stem: A company runs batch jobs that do heavy mathematical calculations and need high CPU performance.

options.why: Compute optimized instances suit CPU-intensive workloads like batch processing and HPC.
These focus on large memory, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
T instances suit low baseline CPU with occasional bursts.
These focus on fast local storage, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

explanation.answer: Compute optimized instances (C family) are ideal for compute-bound applications such as batch processing, gaming servers and scientific modeling.
explanation.concept: Match instance families to the workload's bottleneck.

stem: A research team trains deep learning models and needs GPUs.
prompt: Which EC2 instance category should it choose?

options.why: These focus on disk I/O, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Accelerated computing instances include GPUs or ML chips.
These focus on RAM, not GPUs, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
General purpose instances don't include GPUs for training.

explanation.answer: Accelerated computing instances (such as P, G, Trn and Inf) use hardware accelerators like GPUs and AWS Trainium for ML and graphics.
explanation.concept: AWS Trainium is for training; AWS Inferentia is for inference.

stem: A company wants to run code when a file is uploaded to S3, without managing servers.

options.why: EC2 requires managing servers, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Batch schedules batch jobs on compute it provisions; it isn't the simplest way to run code on each upload event.
Lambda runs code in response to events, such as S3 uploads, without servers to manage.
Outposts runs AWS on premises, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

explanation.answer: AWS Lambda runs your code in response to events and automatically manages the compute resources.
explanation.concept: You pay for requests and compute time; functions can run for up to 15 minutes.

stem: A company wants to run Docker containers on AWS using an AWS-native orchestration service.

options.why: Lightsail offers simple hosting, not AWS's main container orchestration service.
Batch can run container jobs but is for batch processing, not general container orchestration.
Lambda runs functions, not a container orchestration service for Docker workloads.
ECS is AWS's fully managed container orchestration service.

explanation.answer: Amazon ECS is a fully managed container orchestration service for running and scaling containerized applications.
explanation.concept: ECS can run containers on EC2 instances or on AWS Fargate.

stem: A company already uses Kubernetes on premises and wants a managed Kubernetes control plane on AWS.

options.why: EKS provides managed Kubernetes on AWS, so it meets the requirement described here.
Lightsail is for simple hosting, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Batch runs batch jobs, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
ECS is AWS's own orchestrator, not Kubernetes.

explanation.answer: Amazon EKS runs the Kubernetes control plane for you, so you can run Kubernetes workloads on AWS.
explanation.concept: EKS supports EC2 nodes and AWS Fargate.

stem: A team wants to run containers without provisioning or managing any EC2 instances.

options.why: This requires managing EC2 instances, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Fargate is serverless compute for containers with ECS or EKS.
Outposts runs AWS on premises, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Lightsail provides virtual servers to manage.

explanation.answer: AWS Fargate removes the need to manage servers for containers. You define CPU and memory per task or pod.
explanation.concept: Fargate works with both Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS.

stem: A web application runs on several EC2 instances, and traffic needs to be spread across them.

options.why: CloudFront caches content at the edge; it doesn't spread requests across a group of instances in a VPC.
Direct Connect links on-premises networks to AWS.
ELB distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets.
Resolver handles DNS resolution within VPCs.

explanation.answer: Elastic Load Balancing distributes traffic across EC2 instances, containers and IP addresses in multiple AZs and checks their health.
explanation.concept: Types include Application Load Balancer (HTTP/HTTPS), Network Load Balancer (TCP/UDP) and Gateway Load Balancer.
explanation.examTip: Spread traffic across instances = Elastic Load Balancing.

stem: A company wants EC2 capacity to increase automatically when CPU usage is high and decrease when it is low.

options.why: ELB distributes traffic; it doesn't add or remove instances.
Compute Optimizer recommends sizes; it doesn't scale capacity automatically.
Beanstalk can manage scaling for apps it deploys, but EC2 Auto Scaling is the service that scales EC2 capacity directly.
Auto Scaling adds and removes instances based on demand.

explanation.answer: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling maintains availability and scales capacity in and out based on policies, schedules or demand.
explanation.concept: It also replaces unhealthy instances automatically.
explanation.examTip: Add/remove instances automatically = EC2 Auto Scaling.

references.title: What is Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling?

stem: A company needs to route HTTP requests to different services based on the URL path, such as /api and /images.
prompt: Which load balancer should it use?

options.why: ALB routes HTTP/HTTPS requests based on content such as paths and host names.
GWLB is for third-party virtual appliances.
Route 53 is DNS, not path-based request routing.
NLB works at the transport layer and doesn't route by URL path.

explanation.answer: The Application Load Balancer operates at layer 7 and supports path-based and host-based routing.
explanation.concept: Choose NLB for extreme performance, TCP/UDP and static IPs.
explanation.examTip: Route by URL path = Application Load Balancer.

references.title: What is an Application Load Balancer?

stem: A small business wants a simple virtual server with a predictable monthly price to host a WordPress site.

options.why: Outposts runs AWS on premises, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Lightsail offers simple virtual servers and bundles with predictable pricing.
Batch runs batch jobs, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
EKS is managed Kubernetes, more complex than needed.

explanation.answer: Amazon Lightsail provides easy-to-use virtual private servers, storage and networking for a low, predictable monthly price.
explanation.concept: It's designed for simple workloads, websites and small apps.
explanation.examTip: Simple site, fixed monthly price = Lightsail.

stem: A research lab needs to run thousands of batch computing jobs and wants AWS to provision the right compute capacity automatically.

options.why: Lightsail is for simple servers, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
This can work but requires building and managing the scheduling yourself.
Batch plans, schedules and runs batch jobs, provisioning compute automatically.
Step Functions orchestrates workflows but doesn't provision and schedule compute for thousands of batch jobs.

explanation.answer: AWS Batch dynamically provisions compute resources based on the volume and requirements of batch jobs.
explanation.concept: Batch can use EC2 (including Spot) or Fargate.
explanation.examTip: Many batch jobs, managed scheduling = AWS Batch.

stem: A team must choose a container platform. It doesn't use Kubernetes today and wants the simplest AWS-native option with no servers to manage.

options.why: This requires the most management, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.

options.text: Amazon EKS on self-managed EC2 nodes
options.why: This adds Kubernetes complexity and server management.
Lambda has a 15-minute limit and isn't a general container platform.
ECS is AWS-native and Fargate removes server management.

explanation.answer: Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate is a simple, serverless way to run containers without Kubernetes or server management.
explanation.concept: Choose EKS when you need Kubernetes compatibility.
explanation.examTip: Simple + no servers + no Kubernetes = ECS on Fargate.

stem: A company wants every new EC2 instance to start with the same hardened operating system and preinstalled agents.

options.why: An AMI contains the OS and software needed to launch identical instances.
Artifact provides compliance reports, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Lifecycle rules manage objects, which isn't what this scenario needs.

options.text: An EBS snapshot attached manually after launch
options.why: Attaching snapshots manually is slow and doesn't define the boot image.

explanation.answer: An Amazon Machine Image (AMI) provides the information required to launch an instance, including the OS and software.
explanation.concept: Golden AMIs help standardize and secure fleets.
explanation.examTip: Same starting image every time = custom AMI.

stem: One EC2 instance behind a load balancer stops responding.
prompt: What does Elastic Load Balancing do?

options.why: ELB doesn't delete instances; Auto Scaling may replace them.

options.text: Stops routing traffic to the unhealthy instance
options.why: Health checks remove failing targets from rotation.
ELB keeps routing to healthy targets, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

options.text: Sends more traffic to the failed instance to restart it
options.why: ELB doesn't restart instances, which isn't what this scenario needs.

explanation.answer: Elastic Load Balancing performs health checks and routes traffic only to healthy targets.
explanation.concept: With Auto Scaling, unhealthy instances can also be replaced automatically.
explanation.examTip: ELB health checks = traffic only to healthy targets.

stem: A team wants to move a nightly job that runs for three hours to AWS Lambda.

options.text: Lambda can't be triggered on a schedule
options.why: Lambda can run on schedules through EventBridge.
Lambda can access S3 with the right permissions.

options.text: Lambda functions can run for at most 15 minutes
options.why: A three-hour job exceeds Lambda's maximum duration.
Lambda supports many languages, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

explanation.answer: Lambda functions have a maximum timeout of 15 minutes. Long jobs suit AWS Batch, ECS on Fargate or Step Functions orchestration.
explanation.concept: Know service limits that drive architecture choices.
explanation.examTip: Over 15 minutes = not a single Lambda invocation.

stem: A company asks what happens to data on an EC2 instance store volume when the instance is stopped.

options.text: The data is moved to Amazon S3 automatically
options.why: Instance store data isn't moved anywhere.

options.text: The data is kept for 30 days
options.why: There's no retention after stop, which isn't what this scenario needs.

options.text: The data is converted into an EBS snapshot
options.why: No automatic snapshot is created, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Instance store is temporary storage tied to the host's lifetime.

explanation.answer: Instance store provides temporary block storage on the host. Data is lost when the instance stops, terminates or the host fails.
explanation.concept: Use Amazon EBS for data that must persist.

stem: A company is choosing compute services.
prompt: Which TWO are serverless compute options? (Select TWO.)

options.why: EC2 instances are servers you manage, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Lightsail provides virtual servers you manage.
Lambda runs code without servers to manage.
Fargate runs containers without managing servers.
Dedicated Hosts are physical servers, which isn't what this scenario needs.

explanation.answer: Serverless compute options include AWS Lambda (functions) and AWS Fargate (containers).
explanation.concept: Serverless means no servers to provision or manage, automatic scaling and pay-per-use.

stem: A company runs a mix of small web servers and development environments with balanced CPU and memory needs.
prompt: Which instance family is the BEST default choice?

options.why: General purpose instances balance compute, memory and networking.
These add GPUs, which aren't needed, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
These are for memory-heavy workloads, which isn't what this scenario needs.
These are for heavy local disk I/O, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.

explanation.answer: General purpose instances provide a balance of compute, memory and networking and suit web servers and dev environments.
explanation.concept: Burstable T instances are cost-effective for low average CPU with occasional spikes.
explanation.examTip: Balanced / don't know yet = general purpose.

stem: A team needs a private place to store and version its Docker container images on AWS.

options.why: CodePipeline orchestrates release pipelines.
ECR is a managed container image registry.
Glacier is archival storage, not a container registry.
EFS is a file system, which isn't what this scenario needs.

explanation.answer: Amazon ECR is a fully managed container registry for storing, sharing and deploying container images.
explanation.concept: ECR integrates with ECS, EKS and Amazon Inspector image scanning.

stem: An architect explains vertical and horizontal scaling.

options.text: Vertical scaling adds instances; horizontal scaling resizes one
options.why: These are reversed, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.

options.text: Both mean moving to a different Region
options.why: Neither is about changing Regions, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.

options.text: Vertical scaling uses a bigger instance; horizontal scaling adds more instances
options.why: Vertical changes size; horizontal changes count.

options.text: Horizontal scaling is only for databases
options.why: Horizontal scaling applies to many tiers.

explanation.answer: Vertical scaling (scaling up) increases the size of a resource. Horizontal scaling (scaling out) adds more resources.
explanation.concept: Horizontal scaling improves fault tolerance and is usually preferred in the cloud.

stem: A company wants to create a secure, scalable HTTPS API front end for its Lambda functions.

options.why: Route 53 is DNS, which isn't what this scenario needs.
A load balancer can front Lambda, but API Gateway adds API features like authorization and throttling.
Direct Connect is private network connectivity.
API Gateway creates, publishes and secures APIs at any scale.

explanation.answer: Amazon API Gateway lets you create REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs that front Lambda functions and other back ends.
explanation.concept: It handles authorization, throttling and monitoring.
explanation.examTip: API front end for Lambda = API Gateway.

stem: A company needs a public IPv4 address that stays the same even when its EC2 instance is stopped and started.

options.why: An Elastic IP is a static public IPv4 address you can attach to instances.
Health checks monitor endpoints, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Private IPs aren't reachable from the internet.
Automatic public IPs change after stop and start.

explanation.answer: An Elastic IP address is a static public IPv4 address allocated to your account that you can associate with an instance.
explanation.concept: Public IPv4 addresses, including Elastic IPs, are billed hourly.

stem: A company's internal reporting app is busy every weekday from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. and almost unused at night and on weekends.
prompt: Which Auto Scaling approach fits this predictable pattern BEST?

options.why: Running peak capacity all the time wastes money at night and on weekends.

options.text: Scheduled scaling actions for business hours
options.why: Scheduled actions change capacity at known times, matching the predictable pattern.

options.text: Move the app to a larger instance type
options.why: A bigger instance doesn't reduce capacity during quiet hours.

options.text: Scale manually each morning and evening
options.why: Manual scaling is error-prone and easy to forget.

explanation.answer: EC2 Auto Scaling supports scheduled actions that set capacity at specific times, ideal for predictable daily or weekly patterns.
explanation.concept: Combine scheduled scaling with dynamic scaling to handle unexpected spikes.

references.title: Scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
